facts.statement: The genus Saurornitholestes was described by Hans-Dieter Sues in 1978.
facts.quote: authority: Sues, 1978

facts.statement: Fossils of Saurornitholestes date to the Late Cretaceous, with possible records extending to the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous, Possible Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary record

facts.statement: Saurornitholestes was a small, bipedal, carnivorous dinosaur with a sickle-like claw on each foot.
facts.quote: Saurornitholestes was a small, bipedal, meat-eating dinosaur, equipped with a sickle-like claw on each foot.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton of Saurornitholestes was discovered in 1974 by amateur paleontologist Irene Vanderloh near Steveville, Alberta.
facts.quote: In 1974, Canadian amateur paleontologist Irene Vanderloh discovered the skeleton of a small theropod near Steveville in Alberta.

facts.statement: Hans-Dieter Sues named the type species Saurornitholestes langstoni in 1978.
facts.quote: In 1978, Sues named and described the specimen as the type species Saurornitholestes langstoni.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in the Dinosaur Park Formation, which dates to the late Campanian stage.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, TMP 1974.10.5, was uncovered in a layer of the Dinosaur Park Formation dating to the late Campanian.

facts.statement: Fossils representing neonate-sized individuals of Saurornitholestes have been reported.
facts.quote: Neonate-sized Saurornitholestes fossils have been reported in the scientific literature.

facts.statement: The species Saurornitholestes sullivani is known from the Kirtland Formation in New Mexico.
facts.quote: Saurornitholestes sullivani is known from the Hunter Wash fauna of the Kirtland Formation in New Mexico, based on the frontal SMP VP-1270.

facts.statement: Saurornitholestes langstoni is the only dromaeosaurid taxon confirmed from the East Coast of North America.
facts.quote: This also makes S. langstoni currently the only dromaeosaurid taxon reported with certainty from the East Coast.

facts.statement: Robert Sullivan named the species Saurornitholestes robustus in 2006 based on a left frontal bone.
facts.quote: In 2006, Robert Sullivan named and described a second nominal species, Saurornitholestes robustus, based on holotype SMP VP-1955, a left frontal.

facts.statement: The holotype of Saurornitholestes robustus dates to about 73 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype was found in the Willow Wash fauna of the Kirtland Formation in New Mexico, dated to about 73 million years ago.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Saurornitholestes robustus is a valid dromaeosaurid, an indeterminate theropod, or a troodontid.
facts.quote: However, a subsequent overview of dromaeosaurid phylogeny asserted that S. robustus lacked dromaeosaurid characters and should be considered an indeterminate theropod, and a study published in 2014 took the conclusion a step further by demonstrating that S. robustus was assignable to Troodontidae based on similarities with troodontids.

facts.statement: The type species Saurornitholestes langstoni measured between 1.3 and 1.8 meters long and weighed between 5 and 22.5 kilograms.
facts.quote: Saurornitholestes was a small dromaeosaur, with the type species S. langstoni measuring about 1.3 - 1.8 m long and weighing approximately between 5 and 22.5 kg.

facts.statement: Saurornitholestes stood approximately 60 centimeters tall at the hip.
facts.quote: At the hip it stood 60 cm tall.

facts.statement: Saurornitholestes resembled Velociraptor by having large, fang-like teeth at the front of its jaws.
facts.quote: It resembles Velociraptor in having large, fanglike teeth in the front of the jaws.

facts.statement: Hans-Dieter Sues originally assigned Saurornitholestes to the family Dromaeosauridae in 1978.
facts.quote: In 1978, Sues assigned Saurornitholestes to the Dromaeosauridae.

facts.statement: Later studies placed Saurornitholestes in the subfamily Velociraptorinae, but a 2009 analysis by Philip J. Currie placed it in the basal clade Saurornitholestinae.
facts.quote: Later studies most often found it a member of the dromaeosaurid Velociraptorinae, but a cladistic analysis by Philip J. Currie in 2009 recovered a position in a more basal dromaeosaurid clade that was named the Saurornitholestinae.

facts.statement: Saurornitholestes sullivani likely had a keen sense of smell, indicated by an unusually large olfactory bulb in its skull.
facts.quote: Saurornitholestes sullivani is thought to have had a keen sense of smell, due to its skull suggesting an unusually large olfactory bulb.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the second premaxillary teeth of Saurornitholestes may have been specialized for preening feathers.
facts.quote: The second premaxillary teeth of (at least) Saurornitholestes, Velociraptor, and Bambiraptor may have been structurally specialized for preening feathers.

facts.statement: Saurornitholestes was a small, bipedal carnivorous dinosaur equipped with a sickle-shaped retractable claw on the second toe of each foot.
facts.quote: Saurornitholestes era un pequeño dinosaurio carnívoro bípedo, equipado con una garra retráctil en forma de hoz en el segundo dedo de cada pie.

facts.statement: Saurornitholestes measured approximately 1.8 meters in length and weighed about 10 kilograms.
facts.quote: Medía aproximadamente 1,8 metros de largo de longitud y de 10 kilogramos de peso.

facts.statement: Saurornitholestes reached a height of 60 centimeters at the hips.
facts.quote: Alcanzaba una altura de 60 centímetros hasta las caderas.

facts.statement: Saurornitholestes was lighter and had longer legs than other dromaeosaurids such as Velociraptor or Dromaeosaurus.
facts.quote: Saurornitholestes era más ligero y tenía las patas más largas que otros dromeosáuridos como Velociraptor o Dromaeosaurus.

facts.statement: Saurornitholestes likely had an excellent sense of smell, as its skull suggests it possessed an unusually large olfactory bulb.
facts.quote: Saurornitholestes debió haber tenido un excelente sentido del olfato, ya que su cráneo sugiere que tuvo un inusual gran bulbo olfativo.

facts.statement: Two of the nine examined Saurornitholestes hand bones were found to have stress fractures.
facts.quote: Two of the nine hand bones examined for stress fractures were found to have them.

facts.statement: Three toothmarks were visible on the inner surface of a Saurornitholestes dentary.
facts.quote: Three toothmarks were visible on the inner "lingual" surface of the dentary.

facts.statement: While the specific maker cannot be identified, the most likely perpetrator of the toothmarks is hypothesized to be a juvenile tyrannosaurid like Gorgosaurus or Daspletosaurus.
facts.quote: Although a specific identification cannot be made, the most likely perpetrator would be a juvenile individual of one of the Dinosaur Park Formation's tyrannosaurids, like Gorgosaurus, or Daspletosaurus.

facts.statement: Saurornitholestes lived during the late Cretaceous period, approximately between 77 and 68 million years ago, from the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivieron a finales del periodo Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 77 a 68 millones de años, desde el Campaniense al Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Saurornitholestes fossils have been found on both sides of the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: Saurornitholestes was found on both sides of the Western Interior Seaway.

facts.statement: The habitat of Saurornitholestes langstoni in Alberta was similar to the Middle West of the United States, consisting of plains and floodplain swamps.
facts.quote: Alberta, the location of Saurornitholestes langstoni, had a habitat similar to the United States Middle West being plains and floodplain swamps.

facts.statement: The genus Saurornitholestes was described by Sues in 1978.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Sues, 1978

facts.statement: The type species of Saurornitholestes is Saurornitholestes langstoni.
facts.quote: type_species: Saurornitholestes langstoni

facts.statement: Saurornitholestes sullivani is a species within the genus Saurornitholestes, described by Jasinski in 2015.
facts.quote: subdivision: Saurornitholestes sullivani Jasinski, 2015

facts.statement: Bambiraptor has been proposed as a synonym of Saurornitholestes by Burnham et al. in 2000.
facts.quote: synonyms: Bambiraptor? Burnham et al., 2000

facts.statement: Two species of Saurornitholestes have been named: Saurornitholestes langstoni in 1978 and Saurornitholestes sullivani in 2015.
facts.quote: Dos especies han sido nombradas, Saurornitholestes langstoni en 1978 y Saurornitholestes sullivani en 2015.

facts.statement: A Canadian amateur paleontologist named Irene Vanderloh discovered a small theropod skeleton near Steveville, Alberta, in 1974.
facts.quote: En 1974, la paleontóloga aficionada canadiense Irene Vanderloh descubrió el esqueleto de un pequeño terópodo cerca de Steveville en Alberta.

facts.statement: Hans-Dieter Sues named and described the type specimen as Saurornitholestes langstoni in 1978.
facts.quote: En 1978, Sues nombró y describió el espécimen como la especie tipo Saurornitholestes langstoni.

facts.statement: The generic name combines the name of the Saurornithoididae group with the Greek word lestes, meaning "thief".
facts.quote: El nombre genérico hace referencia a los Saurornithoididae, debido al parecido con este grupo que hoy se considera parte de los Troodontidae y combina su nombre con un griego lestes, "ladrón".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen TMP 1974.10.5 was found in the Late Campanian layers of the Dinosaur Park Formation.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo, TMP 1974.10.5, fue descubierto en una capa de la Formación Dinosaur Park que data del Campaniano tardío.

facts.statement: Today, two more complete partial skeletons (RTMP 88.121.39 and MOR 660), dozens of isolated bones, and dozens of teeth are known from the badlands of Dinosaur Provincial Park in Alberta.
facts.quote: Hoy se conocen dos esqueletos parciales más completos y más grandes, RTMP 88.121.39 y MOR 660, docenas de huesos aislados y decenas de dientes en las tierras baldías del Dinosaur Provincial Park en Alberta.

facts.statement: Fossils attributed to Saurornitholestes langstoni have been found in the Oldman Formation dating to about 77 million years ago and the Dos Medicinas Formation dating to about 72 million years ago.
facts.quote: Por ejemplo, la Formación Oldman, que data de hace unos 77 millones de años y la Formación Dos Medicinas hace unos 72 millones de años y de las formaciones Foremost de Alberta y en Río Judith.

facts.statement: Possible indeterminate fossils of Saurornitholestes are known from the Hell Creek Formation in Montana, North Dakota, and South Dakota, dating to about 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Se conocen posibles fósiles indeterminados de la Formación Hell Creek en Montana , Dakota del Norte y Dakota del Sur, que datan de hace unos 66 millones de años.

facts.statement: Fragmentary fossils of Saurornitholestes have also been found in eastern North America.
facts.quote: También se han encontrado fósiles fragmentarios de Saurornitholestes en la mitad oriental de América del Norte.

facts.statement: In 2015, Schwimmer et al. identified Saurornitholestes langstoni in the Tar Heel, Coachman, and Donoho Creek formations of North and South Carolina based on diagnostic teeth and a pedal ungual.
facts.quote: En 2015, Schwimmer et al. identificó la existencia de Saurornitholestes langstoni de las formaciones Tar Heel , Coachman y Donoho Creek de Carolina del Norte y del Sur con base en dientes de diagnóstico y un ungual del pedal.

facts.statement: In 2019, Currie and Evans announced that Zapsalis teeth from the Dinosaur Park Formation represented the second premaxillary tooth of S. langstoni.
facts.quote: Currie y Evans anunciaron en 2019 que los dientes de Zapsalis de la Formación Dinosaur Park representaban el segundo diente premaxilar de S. langstoni.

facts.statement: The second species, Saurornitholestes sullivani, is known from the Hunter Wash fauna of the Kirtland Formation in New Mexico, based on the frontal bone SMP VP-1270.
facts.quote: La segunda especie, Saurornitholestes sullivani, es conocida de la fauna Hunter Wash de la Formación Kirtland en Nuevo México, basado en el frontal SMP VP-1270.

facts.statement: Saurornitholestes sullivani was described and named in 2015 by Steven E. Jasinski.
facts.quote: Fue descripta y nombrada en 2015 por Steven E. Jasinski.

facts.statement: A species formerly assigned to the genus, Saurornitholestes robustus, was described by Sullivan in 2006, though it is now believed to deserve its own genus.
facts.quote: Una especie anteriormente asignada al género, Saurornitholestes robustus fue descrita por Sullivan en 2006, aunque ahora se cree que debería tener su género propio.

facts.statement: The holotype of S. robustus was found in the Willow Wash fauna of the Kirtland Formation in New Mexico, dated to about 73 million years ago.
facts.quote: El holotipo se encontró en la fauna de Willow Wash de la Formación Kirtland en Nuevo México, fechada hace unos 73 millones de años.

facts.statement: In 1978, Sues assigned Saurornitholestes to Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: En 1978, Sues asignó a Saurornitholestes a Dromaeosauridae.

facts.statement: Later studies often placed it in Velociraptorinae, but a 2009 cladistic analysis by Philip J. Currie recovered a position in a more basal dromaeosaurid clade called Saurornitholestinae.
facts.quote: Estudios posteriores lo encontraron con mayor frecuencia como miembro del dromeosáurido Velociraptorinae, pero un análisis cladístico realizado por Philip J. Currie en 2009 recuperó una posición en un clado de dromeosáurido más basal que se llamó Saurornitholestinae.

facts.statement: A 2019 analysis by Philip J. Currie and David C. Evans recovered Saurornitholestes as the sister taxon to Atrociraptor.
facts.quote: El cladograma a continuación es el resultado de un análisis de 2019 realizado por Philip J. Currie y David C. Evans. Currie y Evans recuperaron a Saurornitholestes como el taxón hermano de Atrociraptor.

facts.statement: The feeding habits of Saurornitholestes were typical of ceratosaurian theropods, using a characteristic "stab and throw" feeding method.
facts.quote: Los hábitos de alimentación de Saurornitholestes era la típica de los terópodos celurosaurianos, con un característico método de alimentación de pinchazo y tirar.

facts.statement: Microwear on the teeth indicated that Saurornitholestes likely preferred larger prey than the troodontids sharing its environment.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, el microdesgaste en los dientes indicó que Saurornitholestes probablemente prefirió presas más grandes que los troodóntidos con los que compartía su entorno.

facts.statement: Teeth of Saurornitholestes have been found embedded in the wing bone of the pterosaur Quetzalcoatlus.
facts.quote: Se han encontrado dientes de Saurornitholestes arraigados en el hueso del ala del pterosaurio Quetzalcoatlus.

facts.statement: Because the pterosaur was much larger than Saurornitholestes, Currie and Jacobsen suggest the theropod fed on the carcass of this animal.
facts.quote: Debido a que el pterosaurio era mucho más grande que Saurornitholestes, Currie y Jacobsen sugieren que el terópodo se habría alimentado del cadáver de este animal.

facts.statement: Saurornitholestes was found on both sides of the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: Saurornitholestes se encontró a ambos lados de la vía marítima interior occidental.

facts.statement: The habitat of S. langstoni in Alberta was similar to the Midwestern United States, consisting of plains and alluvial plain swamps.
facts.quote: Alberta, la ubicación de Saurornitholestes langstoni, tenía un hábitat similar al del Medio Oeste de los Estados Unidos al ser llanuras y pantanos de llanuras aluviales.

facts.statement: Saurornitholestes lived alongside hadrosaurs like Eotrachodon and Hypsibema, large theropods like Appalachiosaurus and Dryptosaurus, an unidentified ornithomimosaur, and another small unidentified theropod likely a dromaeosaurid or troodontid.
facts.quote: Saurornitholestes vivía junto a hadrosáuridos como Eotrachodon e Hypsibema, grandes terópodos como Appalachiosaurus y Dryptosaurus, un ornitomimosauriano no identificado y otro pequeño terópodo no identificado que probablemente era un dromeosáurido o un troodóntido.

facts.statement: Saurornitholestes appears to have been the most common small theropod in Dinosaur Provincial Park, with its teeth and bones being much more common than those of its massive contemporary, Dromaeosaurus.
facts.quote: Saurornitholestes parece haber sido el terópodo pequeño más común en el Parque Provincial de Dinosaurios y los dientes y huesos son mucho más comunes que los de su contemporáneo más masivo, Dromaeosaurus.

facts.statement: G. S. Paul concluded that Saurornitholestes is a more modern synonym of Velociraptor, though this is debated.
facts.quote: aunque G. S. Paul concluye que Saurornitholestes es un sinónimo más moderno del Velociraptor.

facts.statement: A later phylogenetic overview claimed S. robustus lacked dromaeosaurid characters and should be considered an indeterminate theropod, while a 2014 study went further to demonstrate it could be assigned to Troodontidae based on similarities with troodontids.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, una descripción general posterior de la filogenia de dromeosáuridos afirmó que S. robustus carecía de caracteres de dromeosáuridos y debería considerarse un terópodo indeterminado, y un estudio publicado en 2014 llevó la conclusión un paso más allá al demostrar que S. robustus se podía asignar a Troodontidae en función de las similitudes con los troodóntidos.

facts.statement: Aase Roland Jacobsen described a dentary of Saurornitholestes in 2001.
facts.quote: Aase Roland Jacobsen publicó una descripción de un dentario de Saurornitholestes en 2001.

facts.statement: The described dentary is about 12 centimeters long and preserves fifteen tooth positions, ten of which retain teeth.
facts.quote: El dentario mide unos 12 centímetros de largo y conserva quince posiciones dentales, de las cuales solo diez conservan dientes.

facts.statement: The striations causing the marks are between 0.37 and 0.40 millimeters thick with cuboidal cross-sections.
facts.quote: Las estrías tienen entre 0,37 y 0,40 milímetros de espesor con secciones transversales cuboidales.

facts.statement: Saurornitholestes belongs to the parent group Saurornitholestinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Saurornitholestinae
